items.explanation_consistent: 해설이 정답·오답 판단과 일치하고 글자 참조가 맞으면 true

items.passage: "Ma'am, this was in the type case," said the boy who brings the paper stock, and he held out my husband's brass composing stick, which I had searched for since the funeral. I confess I was short with him. I believed, as widows are inclined to believe, that every hand in the press room of Port of Spain was waiting to carry off some piece of my husband's trade. Yet the boy did not leave. He asked, with a gravity beyond his years, whether the stick was set to the width of the Gazette or the hymn sheets, for he had noticed the measure was odd. No one but my husband had ever asked me such a question. I showed him. He set three lines of type, slowly and with many errors, and corrected each himself before I could point it out. My sister-in-law, Pearl, says I have taken a stray into the business. Perhaps I have. The boy comes at seven each morning now, and the composing stick is never where I left it, and I no longer search.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the delivery boy?
options: Initial suspicion that gives way to grudging respect and warmth
Lasting distrust masked by polite gratitude for the boy's help
Pity for the boy's poverty mixed with impatience at his errors
Indifference toward the boy until Pearl insists that he be hired
items.explanation: 화자는 처음에 인쇄소의 모든 손이 남편의 물건을 노린다고 믿어 소년에게 퉁명스럽게 대했다고 고백한다. 그러나 소년이 남편만 하던 질문을 하고 스스로 오류를 고치는 모습을 본 뒤, 매일 아침 오는 그를 받아들이고 더 이상 막대를 찾지 않는다. 이처럼 의심이 마지못한 존중과 따뜻함으로 바뀌므로 A가 정답이다. B는 불신이 지속된다고 보았고, C의 동정이나 D의 무관심과 Pearl의 고용 강요는 지문에 근거가 없다.

items.passage: Three times Tendai invited me to supper, and three times I refused, each time with a reason that sounded better on the stair than it had in my head. We shared a wall, Tendai and I, in a narrow house near the Company's Garden, and through that wall I heard her sing while she cooked, badly and with great happiness. I told myself I was too busy. In truth I was a widow of one year, and a table set for two seemed to me a kind of trap. I took to spending evenings in the reading room of the public library, where silence was not only allowed but required. One night I looked up from my book and saw Tendai at the next table, reading a cookery manual with a pencil behind her ear. She did not invite me again. She only slid a slip of paper across the table: a list of dishes, with a question mark beside each. I have kept it, though I am ashamed to say how long I took to answer. The reading lamps in that room were green, and they hummed when the trams went by.
items.question: Which choice best describes the narrator Sunethra's attitude in the text?
options: Lingering resentment of Tendai for intruding on her private grief
Rueful self-awareness about her refusals and fondness for Tendai
Amused contempt for Tendai's poor singing and clumsy cooking
Proud satisfaction at having protected her solitude successfully
items.explanation: 화자는 거절 이유가 머릿속보다 계단에서 더 그럴듯하게 들렸다고 말하며, 사실은 2인용 식탁이 덫처럼 느껴졌다고 스스로를 돌아본다. 또 Tendai의 노래를 '서툴지만 아주 행복하게'라고 표현하고, 그녀가 건넨 쪽지를 간직하며 늦게 답한 것을 부끄러워한다. 이 단서들을 연결하면 자신의 거절에 대한 씁쓸한 자각과 Tendai에 대한 애정이 드러나므로 B가 정답이다. A의 원망, C의 경멸, D의 자부심은 화자의 태도와 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Steam from the barley tea, the tick of the old refrigerator, the smell of rain on the volcanic stone outside: Jiwoo noticed all of it because she could not bear to notice the score on the table. Bruno had asked to see the sonata she had been composing for two years, and she had brought only the first movement, the one she had rewritten eleven times. He read it in silence. In lessons he was merciless about a single wavering note. Now he said only, "Where is the rest?" She told him it was not ready. He set the pages down and showed her his own notebook, its margins full of half-finished melodies dated decades back. "Neither was mine," he said. The landlady came in then, shaking out an umbrella, and set a bowl of tangerines by the sink.
items.question: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
options: To recount a lesson in which Bruno corrects the errors in Jiwoo's first movement
To describe the atmosphere of a rainy boarding-house kitchen on Jeju Island
To suggest that every artist must eventually abandon some creative work
To show a demanding teacher easing a student's fear of sharing unfinished work
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 곳의 근거를 합쳐 요지를 잡아야 하고, 오답 하나는 일화 요약에 그치는 부분 요지다
items.explanation: 앞부분에서 Jiwoo는 악보를 차마 보지 못하고 1악장만 열한 번 고쳐 가져올 만큼 미완성 작품을 보여 주기를 두려워한다. 뒷부분에서 평소 흔들리는 음 하나에도 가차 없던 Bruno는 수십 년 된 미완성 선율로 가득한 자신의 공책을 보여 주며 '내 것도 그랬다'고 말한다. 이 대비를 통해 엄격한 스승이 학생의 두려움을 덜어 주는 장면임이 드러나므로 D가 정답이다. A는 실제로 교정하지 않으므로 틀리고, B는 배경 묘사에 그치며, C는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.

items.passage: Cape Town had turned cold for the funeral, and in their grandmother's yard the hives sat under sheets like furniture in a closed house. Harriet pressed a parcel into Rangi's hands before the mourners had finished their tea. Inside was a jar of honey with a hand-lettered label: Orange Blossom, Gran's last harvest. Rangi knew at once that it was not; the hives had been empty since winter, and the lid came from the supermarket. He held the jar to the window anyway and said the color was exactly right. Harriet smiled too widely and agreed. Later, when an aunt asked to taste it, Rangi said he was saving it, and Harriet looked at him with something close to gratitude. Along the fence, a row of agapanthus nodded blue heads against the wet brick.
items.question: Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
options: Harriet gives Rangi a jar of honey at their grandmother's funeral gathering.
Two cousins quietly sustain a well-meant pretense for each other's sake.
The grandmother's beekeeping declined steadily during her final winter.
Grief makes every family gathering awkward for the people who attend.
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 곳의 근거를 합쳐 요지를 잡아야 하고, 오답 하나는 일화 요약에 그치는 부분 요지다
items.explanation: Rangi는 꿀이 할머니의 마지막 수확이 아니라는 것을 알면서도 색이 딱 맞다며 맞장구친다. 뒤에서 이모가 맛보려 하자 아껴 두겠다고 막아 주고 Harriet이 고마워하는 듯 바라보므로, 두 사촌이 서로를 위해 선의의 연기를 함께 지켜 가는 것이 요지인 B가 정답이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, C는 벌통 소재를 쓰지만 목적이 다르며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 진술이다.

items.passage: Steam and the smell of frying garlic filled the galley where I mended the crew's uniforms while our ship sat in Shanghai for repairs. Meilin, my only apprentice, worked across the table on a torn cuff. That morning the cook, Burak, had burned his hand, and we had both seen it happen. By noon the captain wanted statements. Meilin said the pan had slipped; I had seen Burak reach for it without a cloth. We argued quietly, needles moving. I assumed she was protecting him. Then she described the angle of the handle and the jolt of the hull against the pier, details I had missed because I had been watching his face. We wrote two accounts and signed both. Outside the porthole, gulls fought over a crust on the black water.
items.question: Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
options: To recount how a ship's cook burned his hand while the vessel was docked
To describe the daily routine of mending uniforms in a crowded ship's galley
To show the narrator realizing that a conflicting account reflected another view
To argue that witnesses should always trust their own eyes over others' words
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 곳의 근거를 합쳐 요지를 잡아야 하고, 오답 하나는 일화 요약에 그치는 부분 요지다
items.explanation: 화자는 처음에 Meilin이 Burak을 감싸려고 다르게 말한다고 여긴다. 그러나 Meilin이 손잡이 각도와 선체의 흔들림처럼 화자가 얼굴을 보느라 놓친 세부를 말하자 두 진술을 모두 서명해 제출하므로, 다른 진술이 거짓이 아니라 다른 시점에서 나왔음을 깨닫는 과정이 핵심인 C가 정답이다. A는 사고 일화만, B는 배경 소재만 말한다. D는 지문의 결론과 반대 방향의 일반론이다.

items.passage: Lucius found his son already in the backyard vineyard the morning after the storm, kneeling where the wind had torn out the oldest vine behind their South Side two-flat. Its roots had pulled up a rusted lunchbox. "Leave it," Lucius said, but the boy had already pried it open. Inside lay a photograph of Lucius at nineteen, grinning on a club stage with a trumpet, and a ticket stub from Forty-Seventh Street. For years Lucius had told his son, who practiced guitar behind a closed door, that music was no way to feed a family. The boy looked at the photograph a long time, then set it on the fence post and began pressing soil back around the roots. Next door, Beulah called over to ask whether the grapes had survived, and Lucius said most of them had.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Lucius most likely tell his son to "Leave it"?
options: He does not want his son to find evidence of a past that contradicts his warnings.
He worries that the oldest vine will die if its roots are disturbed any further.
He wants his son to replant the vine before Beulah notices the storm damage.
He suspects the rusted lunchbox belonged to an earlier owner of the two-flat.
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 단서를 두 문장 이상 연결해야 하며 오답 중 하나는 결과를 동기로 착각하는 전형적 오독이다
items.explanation: 상자 안에는 열아홉 살의 Lucius가 트럼펫을 들고 무대에 선 사진이 있었다. 바로 이어 그가 수년간 아들에게 음악으로는 가족을 먹여 살릴 수 없다고 말해 왔다는 문장이 나오므로, 두 문장을 이어 읽으면 자신의 말과 모순되는 과거를 들키고 싶지 않았다는 A가 정답이다. B는 지문에 없는 다른 걱정, C는 이후 행동을 동기로 착각한 것, D는 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.

items.passage: Nobody had expected Kenji to come. The fishing season had been the worst in twenty years, and in October he had told Sakura he would leave her boat for a factory job in Sapporo. Yet here he stood at the back of the crowded wedding hall in a borrowed suit, holding a gift wrapped in newspaper. Sakura, who had taught him to mend nets since he was fifteen, watched him search the crowd until he found her nephew, the groom. Kenji had once told her that the boy was the only one in the harbor who never laughed at his clumsy knots. He handed over the parcel, bowed deeply, and slipped out before the speeches. Snow had begun falling on the parking lot, softening the outlines of the delivery vans.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Kenji most likely attend the wedding?
options: He hopes to persuade Sakura to let him return to work on her boat.
He wants to honor the groom, who was kind to him when others mocked him.
He needs to deliver a gift on behalf of his new factory in Sapporo.
He wishes to apologize to the harbor for the season's poor catch.
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 단서를 두 문장 이상 연결해야 하며 오답 중 하나는 결과를 동기로 착각하는 전형적 오독이다
items.explanation: Kenji는 식장에서 신랑을 찾아 선물을 건넨 뒤 곧바로 떠난다. 바로 다음 문장에서 그가 신랑을 항구에서 유일하게 자신의 서툰 매듭을 비웃지 않은 사람이라고 말했다는 단서가 나오므로, 그 친절에 대한 감사를 표하러 왔다는 B가 정답이다. A는 배와 관련된 다른 바람, C는 지문에 없는 외부 이유, D는 흉어기라는 소재를 엉뚱하게 동기로 바꾼 선택지다.

items.passage: Kerala's monsoon was drumming on the tin roof of the school music room when Arjun found me there, tuning the harmonium I had sold him a year before. I run the instrument shop by the bus stand, and the school calls me for repairs. All that spring Arjun had come into my shop each week, insisting that the harmonium's flat reed had cost his daughter her place in the state competition. Every time, I had refused to admit fault. That afternoon he did not mention the competition. Instead he pointed to Theo, a boy who would compete next month on an instrument no better than his daughter's, and asked whether I could teach him to hear a reed going flat before a judge did. I said yes before I had decided to. Rain kept pooling under the door, and the caretaker laid sacks across the threshold.
items.question: Based on the text, why does Arjun most likely ask the narrator to help Theo?
options: He wants to force the narrator to finally admit that the harmonium was at fault.
He hopes to earn a refund for his daughter by bringing the shop a new customer.
He wants to keep another young player from losing to a flaw no one noticed.
He has been asked by the school to find a qualified music teacher for Theo.
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 단서를 두 문장 이상 연결해야 하며 오답 중 하나는 결과를 동기로 착각하는 전형적 오독이다
items.explanation: Arjun은 음이 낮아진 리드 때문에 딸이 대회에서 떨어졌다고 믿어 왔다. 이어서 Theo가 딸의 것만큼 나쁜 악기로 다음 달 대회에 나간다는 점과 심사위원보다 먼저 리드 문제를 듣게 가르쳐 달라는 부탁이 나오므로, 두 단서를 이어 보면 같은 일이 다른 아이에게 반복되지 않게 하려는 C가 정답이다. A는 그가 과거에 품었던 다른 감정, B는 지문에 없는 이익, D는 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.

items.passage: By six the bus to the hills was already late, and Dolores stood under the shelter with a cement-gray handprint still on her shirt. That morning, in front of the whole crew, she had backed the mixer into the site office and knocked the foreman's lunch off the windowsill. Armand had stared at the spilled rice for a long moment. Now he arrived at the stop, set down his bag, and offered her half of a roti he had bought to replace it. "Office needed a new door anyway," he said. She laughed, then covered her mouth, still half ashamed, and he laughed louder so that she would not have to stop. Below them the lights of Port of Spain came on in loose strings, and a dog trotted past with great purpose.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
options: Anxious and embarrassed, dwelling mainly on the young worker's mistake
Mostly embarrassed, with only a passing hint of the foreman's kindness
Nostalgic, recalling the city's evenings from a great distance in time
Warmly humorous, with traces of lingering embarrassment
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 정서의 비중을 판단해야 하며, 오답은 정반대가 아니라 비중이 틀린 어조다
items.explanation: 지문에는 Dolores가 동료들 앞에서 실수한 일과 여전히 반쯤 부끄러워 입을 가리는 모습이 있지만, 더 두드러지는 것은 Armand가 로티를 나눠 주며 농담하고 그녀가 웃음을 멈추지 않도록 더 크게 웃어 주는 따뜻한 유머다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 덜 두드러진 정서인 당혹감만 말했고, B는 두 정서의 비중을 뒤집었다. C의 향수는 지문에 단서가 약하다.

items.passage: Mumbai was still gray when Tara let herself into her uncle's bakery through the back door, the ovens ticking as they warmed. Coach Riccardo was already there, as he was every Saturday, buying pav for the team. He did not look up from the trays. So the rumor had reached him: that she had called his lineup a joke in front of the selectors. She had said the words, though not about him. Tara tied on an apron and began dusting loaves, flour rising in small clouds, and the silence stretched until her hands ached from working. At last Riccardo asked whether the cardamom buns were fresh. She said they would be in ten minutes. He said he would wait. Outside, a delivery boy leaned his bicycle against the shutter and counted coins into his palm.
items.question: Which choice best describes the overall mood of the text?
options: Tense and uneasy, though softened by a tentative hint of reconciliation
Quietly hopeful, as two old friends look forward to a warm reunion
Mostly at ease, though briefly interrupted by a flicker of strain
Festive and bustling, in keeping with a busy morning at a city bakery
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 정서의 비중을 판단해야 하며, 오답은 정반대가 아니라 비중이 틀린 어조다
items.explanation: Riccardo가 고개를 들지 않고 침묵이 손이 아플 만큼 길게 이어지는 장면은 긴장과 불편함을 주된 분위기로 만든다. 그러나 그가 빵이 신선한지 묻고 기다리겠다고 말하는 부분에서 화해의 조심스러운 기미가 비치므로 A가 정답이다. B는 덜 두드러진 희망만 말했고, C는 두 정서의 비중을 뒤집었으며, D의 떠들썩함은 지문에 단서가 거의 없다.

items.passage: Because a flooded road was holding up the buses, Niamh and Rory were the only two left in the camp dining hall in Galway, each at the far end of a long table. They had not spoken all week. Rory broke the silence by saying that a counselor had told him he played the fiddle "like someone apologizing." Niamh laughed, then stopped, and admitted that a teacher had once said the same about her singing, years ago, and she had not sung since. Rory slid his fiddle case down the table toward her. "Then you can sing badly while I play badly," he said, and she moved three seats closer. Rain streamed down the tall windows, and somewhere in the kitchen someone was stacking trays one at a time.
items.question: Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between Niamh and Rory?
options: Rory pities Niamh, who resents him for prying into her painful past.
Niamh offers to coach Rory, who is anxious about his fiddle playing.
Two near-strangers discover a shared hurt and begin to encourage each other.
Longtime camp rivals compete over which of them has more musical talent.
items.recipeBeyondMedium: 두 문장의 단서를 연결해야 하고 오답은 한쪽 감정만 반영한다
items.explanation: Rory가 상담사에게 들은 말을 털어놓자 Niamh도 선생님에게 같은 말을 듣고 노래를 그만두었다고 고백한다. 이어 Rory가 바이올린 케이스를 밀어 주며 함께 서툴게 해 보자고 하고 Niamh가 세 자리 다가앉으므로, 같은 상처를 확인한 두 사람이 서로를 격려하기 시작하는 관계인 C가 정답이다. A는 한쪽 감정만 지어냈고, B는 격려의 방향을 뒤집었으며, D는 지문에 없는 경쟁 관계라는 통념이다.

items.passage: Folasade read the last of their mother's letters aloud while Obinna sat by the guesthouse window, where the monks' bell rope hung motionless in the noon heat of Dakar. The plan had succeeded: the house in Lagos was sold, the debts were paid, and their mother would join them before the rains. Every letter said she was grateful. Not one said she was glad. Between the final pages Folasade found a pressed hibiscus, faded to the color of weak tea, which their mother had always picked from the vine beside the old front door. Obinna turned it over in his palm and remarked that the new house had no such vine. "We can plant one," Folasade said. He laid the flower on the windowsill, and neither of them moved to return it to the envelope, though the breeze kept nudging it toward the edge.
items.question: In the text, the pressed hibiscus most likely represents
options: the debts that the sale of the house in Lagos has finally settled.
the quiet routine of the monks that the siblings hope to imitate.
the new house that the mother will soon share with her children.
the attachment to home that the mother gave up for the siblings' plan.
items.explanation: 히비스커스는 어머니가 옛집 현관 옆 덩굴에서 늘 따던 꽃이고, 편지에는 고맙다는 말만 있을 뿐 기쁘다는 말은 없다. Obinna가 새집에는 그런 덩굴이 없다고 말하는 대목까지 이어 보면, 이 꽃은 계획을 위해 어머니가 포기한 집에 대한 애착을 나타내므로 D가 정답이다. A는 매각의 결과, B는 배경 소재, C는 꽃과 반대되는 새집을 가리켜 맞지 않는다.

items.passage: Astrid did not believe in new gates. For forty years she had repaired the oak gate of the cemetery in Bergen, replacing one rotten slat at a time, so that by now hardly a board of the original remained. Her apprentice, Anahera, wanted to mark the gate's hundredth year with something grand: a carved arch, the town's name in gold leaf. Astrid only handed her a plane and a single slat cut from the same stand of oak. "One board," she said. "Each year, one board." Anahera fitted it beside a slat that Astrid's own teacher had set, and the grain of the two ran nearly together. That evening the gate swung shut behind the last mourners, and the hinges, oiled that morning, made no sound at all.
items.question: In the text, the cemetery gate most likely symbolizes
options: a tradition kept alive through small renewals passed between generations.
the private grief of the mourners who visit the cemetery every evening.
Anahera's desire to bring bold and visible changes to the old town.
the gradual decline of careful craftsmanship in a modernizing city.

### lit40-medium-04-097 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]
"Ma'am, this was in the type case," said the boy who brings the paper stock, and he held out my husband's brass composing stick, which I had searched for since the funeral. I confess I was short with him. I believed, as widows are inclined to believe, that every hand in the press room of Port of Spain was waiting to carry off some piece of my husband's trade. Yet the boy did not leave. He asked, with a gravity beyond his years, whether the stick was set to the width of the Gazette or the hymn sheets, for he had noticed the measure was odd. No one but my husband had ever asked me such a question. I showed him. He set three lines of type, slowly and with many errors, and corrected each himself before I could point it out. My sister-in-law, Pearl, says I have taken a stray into the business. Perhaps I have. The boy comes at seven each morning now, and the composing stick is never where I left it, and I no longer search.

[질문] Which choice best describes the narrator's attitude toward the delivery boy?
A) Initial suspicion that gives way to grudging respect and warmth
B) Lasting distrust masked by polite gratitude for the boy's help
C) Pity for the boy's poverty mixed with impatience at his errors
D) Indifference toward the boy until Pearl insists that he be hired

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
화자는 처음에 인쇄소의 모든 손이 남편의 물건을 노린다고 믿어 소년에게 퉁명스럽게 대했다고 고백한다. 그러나 소년이 남편만 하던 질문을 하고 스스로 오류를 고치는 모습을 본 뒤, 매일 아침 오는 그를 받아들이고 더 이상 막대를 찾지 않는다. 이처럼 의심이 마지못한 존중과 따뜻함으로 바뀌므로 A가 정답이다. B는 불신이 지속된다고 보았고, C의 동정이나 D의 무관심과 Pearl의 고용 강요는 지문에 근거가 없다.
### lit40-medium-04-098 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 narrator_attitude
[지문]
Three times Tendai invited me to supper, and three times I refused, each time with a reason that sounded better on the stair than it had in my head. We shared a wall, Tendai and I, in a narrow house near the Company's Garden, and through that wall I heard her sing while she cooked, badly and with great happiness. I told myself I was too busy. In truth I was a widow of one year, and a table set for two seemed to me a kind of trap. I took to spending evenings in the reading room of the public library, where silence was not only allowed but required. One night I looked up from my book and saw Tendai at the next table, reading a cookery manual with a pencil behind her ear. She did not invite me again. She only slid a slip of paper across the table: a list of dishes, with a question mark beside each. I have kept it, though I am ashamed to say how long I took to answer. The reading lamps in that room were green, and they hummed when the trams went by.

[질문] Which choice best describes the narrator Sunethra's attitude in the text?
A) Lingering resentment of Tendai for intruding on her private grief
B) Rueful self-awareness about her refusals and fondness for Tendai
C) Amused contempt for Tendai's poor singing and clumsy cooking
D) Proud satisfaction at having protected her solitude successfully

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
화자는 거절 이유가 머릿속보다 계단에서 더 그럴듯하게 들렸다고 말하며, 사실은 2인용 식탁이 덫처럼 느껴졌다고 스스로를 돌아본다. 또 Tendai의 노래를 '서툴지만 아주 행복하게'라고 표현하고, 그녀가 건넨 쪽지를 간직하며 늦게 답한 것을 부끄러워한다. 이 단서들을 연결하면 자신의 거절에 대한 씁쓸한 자각과 Tendai에 대한 애정이 드러나므로 B가 정답이다. A의 원망, C의 경멸, D의 자부심은 화자의 태도와 맞지 않는다.
### lit40-medium-04-100 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose
[지문]
Steam from the barley tea, the tick of the old refrigerator, the smell of rain on the volcanic stone outside: Jiwoo noticed all of it because she could not bear to notice the score on the table. Bruno had asked to see the sonata she had been composing for two years, and she had brought only the first movement, the one she had rewritten eleven times. He read it in silence. In lessons he was merciless about a single wavering note. Now he said only, "Where is the rest?" She told him it was not ready. He set the pages down and showed her his own notebook, its margins full of half-finished melodies dated decades back. "Neither was mine," he said. The landlady came in then, shaking out an umbrella, and set a bowl of tangerines by the sink.

[질문] Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
A) To recount a lesson in which Bruno corrects the errors in Jiwoo's first movement
B) To describe the atmosphere of a rainy boarding-house kitchen on Jeju Island
C) To suggest that every artist must eventually abandon some creative work
D) To show a demanding teacher easing a student's fear of sharing unfinished work

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
앞부분에서 Jiwoo는 악보를 차마 보지 못하고 1악장만 열한 번 고쳐 가져올 만큼 미완성 작품을 보여 주기를 두려워한다. 뒷부분에서 평소 흔들리는 음 하나에도 가차 없던 Bruno는 수십 년 된 미완성 선율로 가득한 자신의 공책을 보여 주며 '내 것도 그랬다'고 말한다. 이 대비를 통해 엄격한 스승이 학생의 두려움을 덜어 주는 장면임이 드러나므로 D가 정답이다. A는 실제로 교정하지 않으므로 틀리고, B는 배경 묘사에 그치며, C는 지나치게 일반적인 교훈이다.
### lit40-medium-05-082 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose
[지문]
Cape Town had turned cold for the funeral, and in their grandmother's yard the hives sat under sheets like furniture in a closed house. Harriet pressed a parcel into Rangi's hands before the mourners had finished their tea. Inside was a jar of honey with a hand-lettered label: Orange Blossom, Gran's last harvest. Rangi knew at once that it was not; the hives had been empty since winter, and the lid came from the supermarket. He held the jar to the window anyway and said the color was exactly right. Harriet smiled too widely and agreed. Later, when an aunt asked to taste it, Rangi said he was saving it, and Harriet looked at him with something close to gratitude. Along the fence, a row of agapanthus nodded blue heads against the wet brick.

[질문] Which choice best states the main idea of the text?
A) Harriet gives Rangi a jar of honey at their grandmother's funeral gathering.
B) Two cousins quietly sustain a well-meant pretense for each other's sake.
C) The grandmother's beekeeping declined steadily during her final winter.
D) Grief makes every family gathering awkward for the people who attend.

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
Rangi는 꿀이 할머니의 마지막 수확이 아니라는 것을 알면서도 색이 딱 맞다며 맞장구친다. 뒤에서 이모가 맛보려 하자 아껴 두겠다고 막아 주고 Harriet이 고마워하는 듯 바라보므로, 두 사촌이 서로를 위해 선의의 연기를 함께 지켜 가는 것이 요지인 B가 정답이다. A는 일화만 요약했고, C는 벌통 소재를 쓰지만 목적이 다르며, D는 지나치게 일반적인 진술이다.
### lit40-medium-05-083 — skill central_ideas_details · 유형 main_idea_or_purpose
[지문]
Steam and the smell of frying garlic filled the galley where I mended the crew's uniforms while our ship sat in Shanghai for repairs. Meilin, my only apprentice, worked across the table on a torn cuff. That morning the cook, Burak, had burned his hand, and we had both seen it happen. By noon the captain wanted statements. Meilin said the pan had slipped; I had seen Burak reach for it without a cloth. We argued quietly, needles moving. I assumed she was protecting him. Then she described the angle of the handle and the jolt of the hull against the pier, details I had missed because I had been watching his face. We wrote two accounts and signed both. Outside the porthole, gulls fought over a crust on the black water.

[질문] Which choice best describes the main purpose of the text?
A) To recount how a ship's cook burned his hand while the vessel was docked
B) To describe the daily routine of mending uniforms in a crowded ship's galley
C) To show the narrator realizing that a conflicting account reflected another view
D) To argue that witnesses should always trust their own eyes over others' words

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
화자는 처음에 Meilin이 Burak을 감싸려고 다르게 말한다고 여긴다. 그러나 Meilin이 손잡이 각도와 선체의 흔들림처럼 화자가 얼굴을 보느라 놓친 세부를 말하자 두 진술을 모두 서명해 제출하므로, 다른 진술이 거짓이 아니라 다른 시점에서 나왔음을 깨닫는 과정이 핵심인 C가 정답이다. A는 사고 일화만, B는 배경 소재만 말한다. D는 지문의 결론과 반대 방향의 일반론이다.
### lit40-medium-05-085 — skill inferences · 유형 character_motivation
[지문]
Lucius found his son already in the backyard vineyard the morning after the storm, kneeling where the wind had torn out the oldest vine behind their South Side two-flat. Its roots had pulled up a rusted lunchbox. "Leave it," Lucius said, but the boy had already pried it open. Inside lay a photograph of Lucius at nineteen, grinning on a club stage with a trumpet, and a ticket stub from Forty-Seventh Street. For years Lucius had told his son, who practiced guitar behind a closed door, that music was no way to feed a family. The boy looked at the photograph a long time, then set it on the fence post and began pressing soil back around the roots. Next door, Beulah called over to ask whether the grapes had survived, and Lucius said most of them had.

[질문] Based on the text, why does Lucius most likely tell his son to "Leave it"?
A) He does not want his son to find evidence of a past that contradicts his warnings.
B) He worries that the oldest vine will die if its roots are disturbed any further.
C) He wants his son to replant the vine before Beulah notices the storm damage.
D) He suspects the rusted lunchbox belonged to an earlier owner of the two-flat.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
상자 안에는 열아홉 살의 Lucius가 트럼펫을 들고 무대에 선 사진이 있었다. 바로 이어 그가 수년간 아들에게 음악으로는 가족을 먹여 살릴 수 없다고 말해 왔다는 문장이 나오므로, 두 문장을 이어 읽으면 자신의 말과 모순되는 과거를 들키고 싶지 않았다는 A가 정답이다. B는 지문에 없는 다른 걱정, C는 이후 행동을 동기로 착각한 것, D는 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.
### lit40-medium-05-086 — skill inferences · 유형 character_motivation
[지문]
Nobody had expected Kenji to come. The fishing season had been the worst in twenty years, and in October he had told Sakura he would leave her boat for a factory job in Sapporo. Yet here he stood at the back of the crowded wedding hall in a borrowed suit, holding a gift wrapped in newspaper. Sakura, who had taught him to mend nets since he was fifteen, watched him search the crowd until he found her nephew, the groom. Kenji had once told her that the boy was the only one in the harbor who never laughed at his clumsy knots. He handed over the parcel, bowed deeply, and slipped out before the speeches. Snow had begun falling on the parking lot, softening the outlines of the delivery vans.

[질문] Based on the text, why does Kenji most likely attend the wedding?
A) He hopes to persuade Sakura to let him return to work on her boat.
B) He wants to honor the groom, who was kind to him when others mocked him.
C) He needs to deliver a gift on behalf of his new factory in Sapporo.
D) He wishes to apologize to the harbor for the season's poor catch.

[표시된 정답] B
[해설]
Kenji는 식장에서 신랑을 찾아 선물을 건넨 뒤 곧바로 떠난다. 바로 다음 문장에서 그가 신랑을 항구에서 유일하게 자신의 서툰 매듭을 비웃지 않은 사람이라고 말했다는 단서가 나오므로, 그 친절에 대한 감사를 표하러 왔다는 B가 정답이다. A는 배와 관련된 다른 바람, C는 지문에 없는 외부 이유, D는 흉어기라는 소재를 엉뚱하게 동기로 바꾼 선택지다.
### lit40-medium-05-087 — skill inferences · 유형 character_motivation
[지문]
Kerala's monsoon was drumming on the tin roof of the school music room when Arjun found me there, tuning the harmonium I had sold him a year before. I run the instrument shop by the bus stand, and the school calls me for repairs. All that spring Arjun had come into my shop each week, insisting that the harmonium's flat reed had cost his daughter her place in the state competition. Every time, I had refused to admit fault. That afternoon he did not mention the competition. Instead he pointed to Theo, a boy who would compete next month on an instrument no better than his daughter's, and asked whether I could teach him to hear a reed going flat before a judge did. I said yes before I had decided to. Rain kept pooling under the door, and the caretaker laid sacks across the threshold.

[질문] Based on the text, why does Arjun most likely ask the narrator to help Theo?
A) He wants to force the narrator to finally admit that the harmonium was at fault.
B) He hopes to earn a refund for his daughter by bringing the shop a new customer.
C) He wants to keep another young player from losing to a flaw no one noticed.
D) He has been asked by the school to find a qualified music teacher for Theo.

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
Arjun은 음이 낮아진 리드 때문에 딸이 대회에서 떨어졌다고 믿어 왔다. 이어서 Theo가 딸의 것만큼 나쁜 악기로 다음 달 대회에 나간다는 점과 심사위원보다 먼저 리드 문제를 듣게 가르쳐 달라는 부탁이 나오므로, 두 단서를 이어 보면 같은 일이 다른 아이에게 반복되지 않게 하려는 C가 정답이다. A는 그가 과거에 품었던 다른 감정, B는 지문에 없는 이익, D는 지문에 없는 외부 원인이다.
### lit40-medium-05-088 — skill inferences · 유형 tone_or_mood
[지문]
By six the bus to the hills was already late, and Dolores stood under the shelter with a cement-gray handprint still on her shirt. That morning, in front of the whole crew, she had backed the mixer into the site office and knocked the foreman's lunch off the windowsill. Armand had stared at the spilled rice for a long moment. Now he arrived at the stop, set down his bag, and offered her half of a roti he had bought to replace it. "Office needed a new door anyway," he said. She laughed, then covered her mouth, still half ashamed, and he laughed louder so that she would not have to stop. Below them the lights of Port of Spain came on in loose strings, and a dog trotted past with great purpose.

[질문] Which choice best describes the overall tone of the text?
A) Anxious and embarrassed, dwelling mainly on the young worker's mistake
B) Mostly embarrassed, with only a passing hint of the foreman's kindness
C) Nostalgic, recalling the city's evenings from a great distance in time
D) Warmly humorous, with traces of lingering embarrassment

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
지문에는 Dolores가 동료들 앞에서 실수한 일과 여전히 반쯤 부끄러워 입을 가리는 모습이 있지만, 더 두드러지는 것은 Armand가 로티를 나눠 주며 농담하고 그녀가 웃음을 멈추지 않도록 더 크게 웃어 주는 따뜻한 유머다. 따라서 D가 정답이다. A는 덜 두드러진 정서인 당혹감만 말했고, B는 두 정서의 비중을 뒤집었다. C의 향수는 지문에 단서가 약하다.
### lit40-medium-05-089 — skill inferences · 유형 tone_or_mood
[지문]
Mumbai was still gray when Tara let herself into her uncle's bakery through the back door, the ovens ticking as they warmed. Coach Riccardo was already there, as he was every Saturday, buying pav for the team. He did not look up from the trays. So the rumor had reached him: that she had called his lineup a joke in front of the selectors. She had said the words, though not about him. Tara tied on an apron and began dusting loaves, flour rising in small clouds, and the silence stretched until her hands ached from working. At last Riccardo asked whether the cardamom buns were fresh. She said they would be in ten minutes. He said he would wait. Outside, a delivery boy leaned his bicycle against the shutter and counted coins into his palm.

[질문] Which choice best describes the overall mood of the text?
A) Tense and uneasy, though softened by a tentative hint of reconciliation
B) Quietly hopeful, as two old friends look forward to a warm reunion
C) Mostly at ease, though briefly interrupted by a flicker of strain
D) Festive and bustling, in keeping with a busy morning at a city bakery

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
Riccardo가 고개를 들지 않고 침묵이 손이 아플 만큼 길게 이어지는 장면은 긴장과 불편함을 주된 분위기로 만든다. 그러나 그가 빵이 신선한지 묻고 기다리겠다고 말하는 부분에서 화해의 조심스러운 기미가 비치므로 A가 정답이다. B는 덜 두드러진 희망만 말했고, C는 두 정서의 비중을 뒤집었으며, D의 떠들썩함은 지문에 단서가 거의 없다.
### lit40-medium-05-091 — skill inferences · 유형 relationship_between_characters
[지문]
Because a flooded road was holding up the buses, Niamh and Rory were the only two left in the camp dining hall in Galway, each at the far end of a long table. They had not spoken all week. Rory broke the silence by saying that a counselor had told him he played the fiddle "like someone apologizing." Niamh laughed, then stopped, and admitted that a teacher had once said the same about her singing, years ago, and she had not sung since. Rory slid his fiddle case down the table toward her. "Then you can sing badly while I play badly," he said, and she moved three seats closer. Rain streamed down the tall windows, and somewhere in the kitchen someone was stacking trays one at a time.

[질문] Based on the text, which choice best describes the relationship between Niamh and Rory?
A) Rory pities Niamh, who resents him for prying into her painful past.
B) Niamh offers to coach Rory, who is anxious about his fiddle playing.
C) Two near-strangers discover a shared hurt and begin to encourage each other.
D) Longtime camp rivals compete over which of them has more musical talent.

[표시된 정답] C
[해설]
Rory가 상담사에게 들은 말을 털어놓자 Niamh도 선생님에게 같은 말을 듣고 노래를 그만두었다고 고백한다. 이어 Rory가 바이올린 케이스를 밀어 주며 함께 서툴게 해 보자고 하고 Niamh가 세 자리 다가앉으므로, 같은 상처를 확인한 두 사람이 서로를 격려하기 시작하는 관계인 C가 정답이다. A는 한쪽 감정만 지어냈고, B는 격려의 방향을 뒤집었으며, D는 지문에 없는 경쟁 관계라는 통념이다.
### lit40-medium-05-092 — skill inferences · 유형 symbolism
[지문]
Folasade read the last of their mother's letters aloud while Obinna sat by the guesthouse window, where the monks' bell rope hung motionless in the noon heat of Dakar. The plan had succeeded: the house in Lagos was sold, the debts were paid, and their mother would join them before the rains. Every letter said she was grateful. Not one said she was glad. Between the final pages Folasade found a pressed hibiscus, faded to the color of weak tea, which their mother had always picked from the vine beside the old front door. Obinna turned it over in his palm and remarked that the new house had no such vine. "We can plant one," Folasade said. He laid the flower on the windowsill, and neither of them moved to return it to the envelope, though the breeze kept nudging it toward the edge.

[질문] In the text, the pressed hibiscus most likely represents
A) the debts that the sale of the house in Lagos has finally settled.
B) the quiet routine of the monks that the siblings hope to imitate.
C) the new house that the mother will soon share with her children.
D) the attachment to home that the mother gave up for the siblings' plan.

[표시된 정답] D
[해설]
히비스커스는 어머니가 옛집 현관 옆 덩굴에서 늘 따던 꽃이고, 편지에는 고맙다는 말만 있을 뿐 기쁘다는 말은 없다. Obinna가 새집에는 그런 덩굴이 없다고 말하는 대목까지 이어 보면, 이 꽃은 계획을 위해 어머니가 포기한 집에 대한 애착을 나타내므로 D가 정답이다. A는 매각의 결과, B는 배경 소재, C는 꽃과 반대되는 새집을 가리켜 맞지 않는다.
### lit40-medium-05-093 — skill inferences · 유형 symbolism
[지문]
Astrid did not believe in new gates. For forty years she had repaired the oak gate of the cemetery in Bergen, replacing one rotten slat at a time, so that by now hardly a board of the original remained. Her apprentice, Anahera, wanted to mark the gate's hundredth year with something grand: a carved arch, the town's name in gold leaf. Astrid only handed her a plane and a single slat cut from the same stand of oak. "One board," she said. "Each year, one board." Anahera fitted it beside a slat that Astrid's own teacher had set, and the grain of the two ran nearly together. That evening the gate swung shut behind the last mourners, and the hinges, oiled that morning, made no sound at all.

[질문] In the text, the cemetery gate most likely symbolizes
A) a tradition kept alive through small renewals passed between generations.
B) the private grief of the mourners who visit the cemetery every evening.
C) Anahera's desire to bring bold and visible changes to the old town.
D) the gradual decline of careful craftsmanship in a modernizing city.

[표시된 정답] A
[해설]
문은 한 번에 한 장씩 판자를 갈아 원래 판자가 거의 남지 않았지만 여전히 같은 문으로 서 있다. Astrid는 화려한 기념물 대신 해마다 한 장씩이라는 방식을 전하고, Anahera의 판자가 Astrid의 스승이 끼운 판자 옆에 결이 이어지듯 놓이므로 문은 세대를 거쳐 조금씩 새로워지며 이어지는 전통을 상징한다. 따라서 A가 정답이다. B와 D는 지문에 근거가 약하고, C는 Astrid가 받아들이지 않은 Anahera의 처음 계획일 뿐이다.
